attribution.statement: The jpark account was used for a console session (workstation#74, 11:14–11:20 UTC) that performed a patients_full export, staging to a hidden temp path, and an unapproved 20.6 MB upload. The account is established as the credential used. The human operator is not established: the badge for the account holder was inside, but the badge check cannot identify who typed, and credentials were previously found written down at the shared station.

summary: Tip: review records access and transfers this shift. Findings: (1) Console session workstation#74 under account jpark (11:14–11:20 UTC) exported patients_full from records (records app export_bulk, corroborated at collector and tap) to /tmp/.font-unix/idx-3e08.bin on workstation. (2) That file was uploaded (~20.58 MB, curl PUT) to 10.20.9.87:8080 at 11:18, which is not an approved bulk destination; this violates the transfer policy. (3) The collector holds the jpark session-74 login line, but workstation's local auth.log lacks it while local records bracket it on both sides; rotation does not explain it (unexplained local absence; who removed it and how is not established). (4) Records access.log gaps before 09:00 are explained by rotation with off-host archive. (5) A 20.58 MB transfer from records to approved stor-nas-01 (10.20.0.45) at 11:59 is policy-consistent and has no overlapping interactive session. Attribution: account jpark was used; the human operator is not established. The jpark badge was inside, but badge records cannot identify who typed, and shared credentials have been found written down before. No person is named or cleared.
open_questions: Who operated the jpark console session at 11:14–11:20 UTC? Requires evidence beyond account and badge data.
How and by whom was the local auth.log entry for session 74 removed? The workstation .1 generation and fs_stat did not show this; not established.
